text:
So far, you made your first prototype of a prosthesis, and you made an automatic machine.

In the next two lessons, you'll connect these things you figured out to make your prosthesis move automatically.

It won't connect to anyone's actual arm yet, but it'll be able to open and close, like the demo gripper did last lesson.
Why would you want to make a prosthesis move automatically before you connect it to someone's actual arm?

Remember, when there's a blue question block like this, it's a reminder to drag it over and answer it in your workspace.

When you drag it, you can delete this text and put your answer here!

Last lesson, you used a demo gripper, but your prostheses are all different - each group made their own design and modifications.

You can make it move by connecting it to a servo. The servo is moves a little gear to different angles. Yours can spin 180 degrees - from up to down.

objects.text: It can move back and forth for 180 degrees (a half circle). Here you see it half way, at 90 degrees.
It can't keep spinning! It can only go from 0 degrees to 180 degrees and back!
This is as far as it can go. Now it can only stay here or go back.
This is its starting point. It can only go in one direction from here.

tiles.title: Figuring out how the servo works in Dataflow

text:
Last lesson, you figured out how the gripper worked in Dataflow. Does the servo work the same way?

Drag this question tile and answer the questions!
What do you notice that is different between the demo gripper and the servo?

How do you think the servo works?

What information do you need to check if your prediction is right?

If you don't have a prediction about the servo, what information do you need to figure out how it works?
